column2: SGLang: Efficient Execution of Structured Language Model Programs
column8: The runtime accelerates execution with novel optimizations like RadixAttention for KV cache reuse
column9: Defines the radix-tree prefix cache (RadixAttention) with LRU leaf eviction that later SGLang work and many papers use as baseline.
column10: Abstract shows benign benchmark programs only; no workload-shift, OOD, overload, or multi-tenant interference evaluation.
column11: Baseline mechanism whose LRU eviction is the thing to stress under mix shift.

column2: Marconi: Prefix Caching for the Era of Hybrid LLMs
column8: novel admission and eviction policies that more judiciously assess potential cache entries
column9: Admission plus eviction beyond LRU for hybrid (SSM+attention) models; reports up to 34.4x token hit-rate gain over prior prefix caching.
column10: Average-case gains on benign traces per abstract; no reported adversarial or shifted-mix test; no tenant interference measurement.
column11: Shows admission control (not just eviction) matters; hybrid-model state makes one-off long prompts costlier to admit.

column2: KVFlow: Efficient Prefix Caching for Accelerating LLM-Based Multi-Agent Workflows
column8: evict KV caches using a Least Recently Used (LRU) policy
column9: Argues LRU fails to anticipate future agent usage; uses workflow step graph to prioritize eviction and prefetch.
column10: Assumes a known agent workflow graph; no test of mispredicted or shifting workflows; no multi-tenant interference.
column11: Workflow-aware eviction relies on structure that breaks under OOD agent behavior; a robustness gap.

column2: KVCache Cache in the Wild: Characterizing and Optimizing KVCache Cache at a Large Cloud Provider
column8: for a specific request category, the pattern tends to be predictable
column9: Alibaba production traces: ideal hit rates 62% and 54% (Traces A/B); single-turn requests give 97% of Trace B hits; reuse time differs by category; daytime vs 3-4 am distributions differ; workload-aware eviction gives 28.3-41.9% QTTFT reduction.
column10: Characterizes diurnal and category variation but the policy is tuned on those traces; no adversarial or OOD category-mix test; no per-tenant isolation measurement.
column11: Strongest production evidence that reuse is category-dependent, so policies keyed on category can be misled by category shift.

column2: Mooncake: A KVCache-centric Disaggregated Architecture for LLM Serving
column8: Mooncake faces challenges due to highly overloaded scenarios
column9: Kimi production system with multi-tier KV pool; explicitly targets overload with prediction-based early rejection.
column10: Overload is handled by rejection; abstract gives no worst-case analysis of the rejection predictor or of hit rate under mix shift; no tenant fairness.
column11: Production admission-control-under-overload precedent tied to KV capacity.

column2: Mooncake FAST'25 Trace Release (README)
column8: Identical hash IDs indicate reusable prefix KV cache blocks.
column9: Public 1-hour conversation (12,031 req, avg input 12,035) and tool/agent (23,608 req, avg input 8,596) traces with 512-token prefix block hashes, enabling hit-rate replay.
column10: One hour only, so no diurnal or long-term shift; anonymized, no tenant IDs, so no multi-tenant interference study possible.
column11: Directly replayable on a laptop to measure eviction-policy hit rate under synthetic mix shifts.

column2: Cost-Efficient Large Language Model Serving for Multi-turn Conversations with CachedAttention
column8: scheduler-aware fetching and eviction schemes
column9: Hierarchical KV caching across GPU/host/disk with scheduler-hinted eviction and prefetch for multi-turn chat.
column10: Benign multi-turn workloads; no evaluation of hint quality under shift or of tier thrash under one-off long prompts; no tenant isolation.
column11: Multi-tier caching depends on scheduler foresight; a lever that degrades when arrivals shift.

column2: Preble: Efficient Distributed Prompt Scheduling for LLM Serving
column8: co-optimizes KV state reuse and computation load-balancing
column9: Cache-aware distributed routing that trades prefix locality against load balance.
column10: Abstract reports benign workloads; no hot-prefix skew shift or adversarial imbalance; no tenant interference.
column11: Cache-aware routing is a second place where shift (hot prefix moves) can cause imbalance.

column2: SkyWalker: A Locality-Aware Cross-Region Load Balancer for LLM Inference
column8: SkyWalker preserves KV-Cache locality and load balancing
column9: Cross-region load balancer with a cache-aware traffic handler and selective pushing.
column10: Focus is regional diurnal load; abstract gives no prefix-popularity-shift stress test or tenant interference measurement.
column11: Cross-region diurnal shift as a driver of KV locality loss.

column2: LMCache: An Efficient KV Cache Layer for Enterprise-Scale LLM Inference
column8: Large-scale adoption of LMCACHE in enterprise settings provides us valuable insights
column9: Open KV offload/sharing layer for vLLM and SGLang; reports context truncation can roughly halve prefix hit ratio in deployments.
column10: Deployment insights, not a controlled shift study; no worst-case or tenant-interference evaluation in abstract.
column11: Evidence that a client-side change (truncation) shifts hit rate sharply: a benign OOD trigger.

column2: BurstGPT: A Real-world Workload Dataset to Optimize LLM Serving Systems
column8: burstiness variations of requests in Azure OpenAI GPT services
column9: Azure OpenAI trace showing diverse concurrency/burst patterns and service failures.
column10: No prefix or KV-block content, so hit-rate shift cannot be measured; no tenant-level interference.
column11: Source of realistic burst arrival processes for stress tests.

column2: ServeGen: Workload Characterization and Generation of Large Language Model Serving in Production
column8: The input and output length distributions shift dynamically and independently over time
column9: Alibaba production study: arrivals bursty with shifting rate and burstiness; length distributions shift over time; a few top clients steer the aggregate workload.
column10: Explicitly says prefix caching was not characterized because request content was withheld; shift is measured but KV hit rate under shift is not.
column11: Direct production evidence of length/KV-demand shift and client dominance; leaves hit-rate shift open.

column2: Azure LLM inference trace 2024 (AzurePublicDataset)
column8: This is a sample of the traces from multiple LLM inference services in Azure, collected on May 10th-19th 2024.
column9: Week-long code and conversation traces with timestamps, context and generated token counts.
column10: No prompt content or prefix hashes, so prefix hit rate cannot be derived; no tenant IDs.
column11: Week-scale diurnal KV-demand (context length x rate) variation input for stress tests.

column2: DynamoLLM: Designing LLM Inference Clusters for Performance and Energy Efficiency
column8: fluctuations in inference workloads
column9: Exploits workload fluctuation for energy-efficient reconfiguration; backs the Azure 2024 trace.
column10: Energy/performance reconfiguration, not KV cache policy; no prefix reuse or tenant interference study.
column11: Context: production fluctuation is large enough to reconfigure clusters around.

column2: Llumnix: Dynamic Scheduling for Large Language Model Serving
column8: live migration mechanism for requests and their in-memory states
column9: Migrates requests and KV state across instances to reduce memory fragmentation and preemption, improve isolation and priority.
column10: Evaluates load imbalance and priorities, but abstract shows no adversarial or OOD mix; isolation is between priorities, not KV quotas per tenant.
column11: Migration is a memory-pressure relief valve; its worst case under correlated surges is untested.

column2: S3: Increasing GPU Utilization during Generative Inference for Higher Throughput
column8: predicts the output sequence length, schedules generation queries based on the prediction
column9: Output-length prediction to reserve KV memory instead of max length, with misprediction handling.
column10: No analysis of predictor under distribution shift (e.g., reasoning models with long outputs); no tenant interference.
column11: KV reservation via prediction is the classic component that fails silently under OOD outputs.

column2: Efficient LLM Scheduling by Learning to Rank
column8: it is possible to predict the relative ranks of output lengths in a batch of requests
column9: Rank-based output-length prediction for SJF-like scheduling.
column10: Benign benchmarks; predictor robustness to shifted prompts not tested in abstract; no tenant isolation.
column11: Predictor-dependent scheduling; candidate for a shift stress test.

column2: InferCept: Efficient Intercept Support for Augmented Large Language Model Inference
column8: unnecessary recomputation of already computed contexts
column9: Chooses among preserve/swap/discard of KV during tool-call interceptions to minimize GPU waste.
column10: Depends on interception duration estimates; no adversarial or shifted tool-latency analysis; no multi-tenant fairness.
column11: Recompute-vs-swap decision under pauses; agent loops are a key shift case.

column2: Fast Distributed Inference Serving for Large Language Models
column8: enable preemption at the granularity of each output token
column9: Token-level preemption with proactive offload/upload of intermediate state to host memory.
column10: No worst-case analysis of offload thrash under memory pressure; no tenant isolation.
column11: Preemption + swap baseline for memory-pressure handling.

column2: Online Scheduling for LLM Inference with KV Cache Constraints
column8: no deterministic online algorithm can achieve a constant competitive ratio
column9: Formal KV-constrained batching model with hindsight-optimal IP benchmark and lower bound for arbitrary arrivals.
column10: Theoretical worst case for scheduling, not prefix-cache hit rate; single tenant.
column11: Worst-case theory exists for KV-constrained scheduling; connects robustness claims to competitive analysis.

column2: Optimizing LLM Inference: Fluid-Guided Online Scheduling with Memory Constraints
column8: overflow can evict in-progress requests
column9: Fluid-model stability region and threshold admission (WAIT, Nested WAIT with safety buffer) for KV memory; tested near/at overload.
column10: Overload tested, but output-length distributions assumed stationary; no prefix-cache interaction; single class.
column11: KV-aware admission control with stability analysis: closest to a robust admission baseline.

column2: Competitive Non-Clairvoyant KV-Cache Scheduling for LLM Inference
column8: a scheduler must minimize latency under a hard memory budget, yet the response lengths of requests are inherently unknown
column9: Prediction-free scheduler with competitive ratio at most 61.92 (32 in large-memory regime).
column10: Worst-case bound on latency, but constant is large and no prefix reuse or multi-tenant model.
column11: Shows robustness without predictors is provable for KV scheduling; gap is prefix-cache-aware version.

column2: Randomization Boosts KV Caching, Learning Balances Query Load: A Joint Perspective
column8: integrate provably competitive randomized KV cache eviction with learning-based methods
column9: Unified model of eviction and routing; competitive randomized eviction plus learned routing.
column10: Competitive guarantee covers eviction in its model; abstract does not show production mix shift or tenant interference.
column11: Closest prior for worst-case-guaranteed prefix eviction; any new robust-eviction claim must beat or extend it.

column2: PRISM: Fast Online LLM Serving via Scheduling-Memory Co-design
column8: align request admission with exact-prefix KV retention
column9: Co-designs admission scheduling with radix-tree retention; 23.3-37.1% lower P99 TTFT per QPS than strongest baseline.
column10: Tail latency measured across load, but no stated OOD or shifted-mix test; no tenant isolation.
column11: Admission-retention coupling is a recent baseline for shift experiments.

column2: PEEK: Predictive Queue-Informed KV Cache Management for LLM Serving
column8: a co-designed eviction hook protects blocks ancestral to queued demand
column9: Uses queued requests to protect needed prefix blocks; gains hold as KV pressure scales on SGLang and vLLM.
column10: Pressure scaled, but workload shift and tenant interference not stated in abstract.
column11: Queue-informed eviction is a cheap robustness lever when queues reflect the shifted mix.

column2: Not All Tokens Are Worth Caching: Learning Semantic-Aware Eviction for LLM Prefix Caches
column8: existing policies such as LRU largely treat cached blocks uniformly
column9: Online-learned eviction by token type with eviction feedback, claimed adaptive to deployment workloads.
column10: Online learning adapts, but abstract gives no bound on regret under abrupt shift or under poisoned feedback; no tenant study.
column11: Learned eviction is exactly where shift robustness (cf. learning-augmented caching) is untested.

column2: A Year in LLM Serving: Workload Evolution, Caching and Load-Balancing
column8: they do not fully capture how LLM serving workloads evolve over time
column9: Year-long trace: output lengths trend down, per-user inter-arrival shrinks (agents), reuse bimodal, LRU/FIFO often match complex policies, ARC underperforms at mid sizes, cache-blind routing replicates prefixes.
column10: Cached-token logging only for final two months, so year-long hit-rate trend is absent; no adversarial test; per-user not per-tenant isolation.
column11: Best evidence on long-term drift; says simple policies are competitive, raising the bar for any new eviction policy.

column2: Continuum: Efficient and Robust Multi-Turn LLM Agent Scheduling with KV Cache Time-to-Live
column8: the method needs to remain robust under limited predictability of tool call durations
column9: Pins agent KV across tool calls with a TTL; evaluated on SWE-Bench and BFCL.
column10: Robustness is to tool-duration noise, not to mixed agent/non-agent tenants competing for KV; no worst-case bound.
column11: TTL pinning can starve other classes under shift; interference is open.

column2: Token Latency Fairness: Performance Isolation for Multi-Tenant LLM Serving
column8: high-demand workloads from one client can cause latency SLO violations for others
column9: FairInference gives latency isolation accounting for delays from the shared KV cache in GPU memory.
column10: Directly measures multi-tenant interference; abstract does not state shift/OOD scenarios beyond high-demand clients.
column11: Closest prior on KV-aware tenant isolation; must be cited and differentiated.

column2: KVShare: An LLM Service System with Efficient and Effective Multi-Tenant KV Cache Reuse
column8: a cache-aware scheduler that prioritizes requests based on their KV cache hit rates
column9: Cross-tenant KV sharing with hit-rate-priority scheduling.
column10: Hit-rate-priority can starve low-hit tenants; no fairness or shift evaluation stated.
column11: Example of a policy whose average gain may create interference under shift.

column2: KV-Cache Wins You Can See: From Prefix Caching in vLLM to Distributed Scheduling with llm-d
column8: Cache-blind schedulers constantly duplicate and evict the same prefixes across different pods.
column9: 150 prefix groups at 73% of cluster KV capacity: precise routing P90 TTFT 0.542 s vs 31.1 s approximate, 92.6 s random.
column10: Single synthetic benign workload; no shift in prefix popularity, no tenant interference.
column11: Shows how steep the TTFT cliff is when cache-aware routing loses state: a degradation magnitude to reuse.

column2: [RFC] Tail-Optimized LRU (T-LRU): Reducing Tail Latency via Conversation-Aware KV Cache Eviction (vllm#37823)
column8: LRU maximizes cache-hit rate but is **conversation-length blind**
column9: Proposes TTFT-budget-aware eviction for vLLM; claims up to 27.4% lower P95 TTFT on real conversations. Issue state CLOSED.
column10: Conversation workloads only; no shift or tenant interference.
column11: Shows upstream interest and that hit-rate-optimal is not tail-optimal.

column2: Tail-Optimized Caching for LLM Inference
column8: a metric of central importance to practitioners
column9: T-LRU proven optimal under a stochastic conversation model; lowers P90/P95 TTFT on WildChat vs LRU.
column10: Optimality is under a stochastic model, not adversarial or shifted; no multi-tenant.
column11: Tail-latency objective for eviction; extending to shift is open.

column2: [Feature] Per-request opt-out from prefix cache insertion (skip_cache_insert) (sglang#38069)
column8: displacing opt-in tenants' real prefixes and lowering their hit rate
column9: Production report that never-hittable inserts occupy radix-tree memory until LRU reaches them, hurting other tenants' hit rate; asks for admission opt-out.
column10: Qualitative; no measurement of the hit-rate loss.
column11: Direct evidence that missing admission control causes cross-tenant KV interference in SGLang.

column2: [RFC] Per-Token-Range KV-Cache Retention Priority (sglang#36208)
column8: Nothing stops the engine from evicting Session A's important prefix to make room for Session B's less-important request
column9: Proposes per-token-range retention priority modeled on TensorRT-LLM KvCacheRetentionConfig.
column10: Design proposal only; no shift or interference measurement.
column11: Shows engines lack retention isolation primitives; priority is soft, not a quota.

column2: L1 eviction races async L2 store: chunks discarded before offload are never stored (LMCache#5350)
column8: ~19% of requests permanently retrieve only the shared prefix
column9: Under L1 memory pressure, eviction races offload so chunks never reach L2, causing persistent re-prefill.
column10: Single-tenant shared-prefix repro; bug, not policy evaluation.
column11: Memory pressure creates a persistent degraded state (metastable-like) in multi-tier KV caches.

column2: FIFO Queues are All You Need for Cache Eviction
column8: most objects in skewed workloads will only be accessed once in a short window
column9: S3-FIFO: small probationary FIFO filters one-hit wonders; lowest mean miss ratio on 10 of 14 datasets over 6594 traces.
column10: Web/KV-store traces, not LLM KV blocks with prefix dependence; robustness is across datasets, not adversarial; no tenant isolation.
column11: One-off long prompts are one-hit wonders; S3-FIFO-style admission is an untested baseline for prefix caches.

column2: SIEVE is Simpler than LRU: an Efficient Turn-Key Eviction Algorithm for Web Caches
column8: SIEVE achieves up to 63.2% lower miss ratio than ARC
column9: Simple lazy-promotion eviction beating ARC on 1559 web traces with lock-free hits.
column10: Web caches; not evaluated on prefix-tree KV with parent-child dependence; no adversarial/tenant study.
column11: Cheap scan-resistant baseline to port to radix KV caches.

column2: ARC: A Self-Tuning, Low Overhead Replacement Cache
column8: allows one-time se-quential requests to pass through without polluting the cache
column9: Scan-resistant, self-tuning balance of recency and frequency.
column10: Storage traces; the 2026 LLM trace study finds ARC below LRU at mid sizes, so scan resistance does not transfer automatically.
column11: Classic answer to the one-off-long-prompt burst; transfer to KV is not guaranteed.

column2: Learning Relaxed Belady for Content Distribution Network Caching
column8: uses machine learning to approximate the Belady MIN algorithm
column9: Learned CDN eviction deployed-feasible, 5-24% WAN traffic reduction.
column10: CDN traces; no guarantee under distribution shift; no multi-tenant isolation.
column11: Template for learned prefix-cache eviction and its shift risk.

column2: Competitive caching with machine learned advice
column8: naively following the oracle's recommendations may lead to very poor performance
column9: Learning-augmented caching with O(log k) worst-case cap regardless of predictor quality.
column10: Uniform-size paging model; no LLM prefix structure or tenants.
column11: Framework for robust learned KV eviction: consistency with good predictions, bounded loss with bad ones.

column2: Metastable Failures in Distributed Systems
column8: a trigger causes the system to enter a bad state that persists even when the trigger is removed
column9: Defines metastable failures; notes the root cause is often features that improve efficiency or reliability.
column10: General distributed systems; no LLM KV measurements.
column11: Frame for KV cache collapse: a burst evicts hot prefixes, misses raise prefill load, which keeps the cache cold.

column2: Metastable Failures in the Wild
column8: categorizing two types of triggers and two types of amplification mechanisms
column9: Empirical study of metastable incidents and amplification mechanisms.
column10: No LLM serving cases.
column11: Gives the taxonomy a KV-cache metastability test would use.

column2: KPart: A Hybrid Cache Partitioning-Sharing Technique for Commodity Multicores
column8: UCP often hurts performance even though its only goal is to improve it
column9: Strict way-partitioning (CAT-style) can lose performance; hybrid clustering then partitioning recovers it.
column10: CPU LLC, not KV; workload assumed profiled.
column11: Analogue: strict per-tenant KV quotas can waste capacity; hybrid share-partition is the lesson.
